headline: Partick narrow favourites in a market that has barely moved
summary: Partick are narrow away favourites at a fair 37.9%, with Dunfermline on 32.2% and the draw on 29.9% in the Scottish Championship. The handicap sits level at +0.11 to the home side, though only five books quote it. Over 2.5 goals is a 46.9% underdog and the fair total is 2.38 goals; Under 2.5 is a narrow 53.1% favourite rather than a settled low-scoring verdict. Both teams to score sits at 52.6% on consensus only. Every move since first seen is rounding or a margin re-cut, and with 17.6 hours of history and three snapshots, the true opening price is unknown. Our reading is low confidence: quiet, not informative.

voices.scout: And that's the story. Partick are narrow away favourites at about thirty-eight per cent, Dunfermline about thirty-two, the draw about thirty. Level ball on the handicap, and a goal expectation of two point three eight. The sharp book hasn't moved a tick on the one-X-two or the handicap in seventeen hours. Sometimes the loudest thing a market says is nothing at all.
voices.sceptic: Careful. The sharp book's Under two and a half drifted from one point seven six to one point seven nine while the Over held at two point oh three. That's a margin re-cut, not money. And no injury news means no injury feed, not a clean bill of health. Three observations in seventeen hours is barely observing a market at all.
voices.gaffer: So we call it what it is. Under two and a half is a narrow fifty-three per cent favourite, not a settled low-scoring verdict. The true opening is unknown, because we only started watching at half past ten on the eighteenth. We call this market quiet and we stay in our seats.
